clue.text: Further information is rejected with glee

indicators.note: being rejected means the little word is sent back, so it is read backwards

parts.note: glee is joy or delight

explanation.surface: Someone's extra news is turned down even though they deliver it gleefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is rejected' turns IS round to SI; DELIGHT follows. A sidelight is incidental information that throws light on a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidelight is a piece of incidental extra knowledge illuminating a topic from the side.

clue.text: Kept going steady

explanation.surface: Something maintained and steady.
explanation.definitionFit: Continued without stopping fits kept going, and constant or unwavering fits steady.

clue.text: Mysterious man died on entrance to lift

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting raises the word so it reads upwards

parts.note: a door is an entrance

explanation.surface: A man of mystery died on the threshold of an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lift' raises DOOR to ROOD in this down clue. Edwin Drood is the hero of Dickens's unfinished The Mystery of Edwin Drood.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's final novel is The Mystery of Edwin Drood, so he is the mysterious figure.

clue.text: Not what made Noel tipsy?

indicators.note: tipsy means drunk, signalling these letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A soft drink could not be what got Noel drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of MADE NOEL is a drink that is not alcoholic, so it cannot be what made him tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemonade is a soft drink, containing no alcohol.

clue.text: A case to concede, covering the point when raised

indicators.note: covering means one word wraps round the other

parts.note: to give is to concede, give way

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word reads upwards

parts.note: a tine is a point or prong, as on a fork or antler

explanation.surface: An argument to give up, getting round the matter once it is brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when raised' turns TINE to ENIT, which goes inside GIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The genitive is the grammatical case expressing possession.

clue.text: Beat husband into pulp

indicators.note: one piece goes into another

parts.note: pulp fiction is trash

explanation.surface: A violent scene: someone beats her husband into a pulp.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash is to beat soundly.

clue.text: Leaves motorway coming out of old European kingdom

indicators.note: the motorway is coming out of the kingdom's name, so its letters are taken away from it

parts.note: Bohemia was a kingdom in central Europe, now part of the Czech Republic
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: Someone drives off the motorway on leaving an old central European realm.
explanation.walkthrough: MI (the M1 motorway, London to Leeds) is removed from BOHEMIA. 'Leaves' looks like a verb but means tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohea is a black China tea, so its leaves are the substance named.

clue.text: Groups of girls are drunk, it's said

indicators.note: it is said indicates a word that sounds like another

parts.note: bevvies is slang for drinks, things that are drunk

explanation.surface: Gossip that crowds of young women are intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: BEVVIES is British slang for alcoholic drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a group, traditionally of women or birds such as quail.

clue.text: King crab found in bays with weed

parts.note: bays are reddish-brown horses
to weed is to hoe

explanation.surface: A large crab is spotted in coastal inlets with seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bays' suggests coastal inlets but means horses; 'found in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The horseshoe crab, named for its shell shape, is also known as the king crab.

clue.text: Range of touring sedan

indicators.note: touring means moving around, so these letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A car on tour covers some mileage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the mountain chain in South America.

clue.text: It could be abominable, yet I joined up

definitions.text: It could be abominable, yet I joined up

parts.words: It could be abominable, yet I joined up
parts.note: the famous Himalayan creature is called abominable, and the words yet and I run together spell the name of that same beast

explanation.surface: A grudging confession: the speaker may be awful, yet still enlisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yet I joined up' gives YETI, also known as the Abominable Snowman; the clue points to the second word of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan yeti is popularly called the Abominable Snowman, so the snow figure is what may be abominable.

clue.text: Highly-regarded priest must remain anonymous…

indicators.note: to stay anonymous is to have no name, and N is the abbreviation for name, so it is dropped

parts.note: a priest is styled the Reverend

explanation.surface: A churchman who is much admired insists that his identity stay secret.
explanation.walkthrough: N (name) leaves REVEREND. The ellipsis joins this clue to the next one in surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Revered means deeply respected or venerated, so it is highly esteemed.

clue.text: …but French department has name for poet

parts.note: the Aude is a department of southern France

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: a French region carries a name for a verse writer instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening '…but' is only a link carrying on the surface of the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden was an Anglo-American writer of verse in the twentieth century.

clue.text: Not giving a smack — it may be offensive

explanation.surface: Something bland has no kick, and it might well give offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Food with no flavour has no smack of anything, and a vulgar joke is offensively lacking in refinement.

clue.text: I have sniffed around before taking the plunge

indicators.note: one piece placed before another in the answer

parts.note: to nose around is to sniff about prying
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone snooped about before committing to a bold leap.
explanation.walkthrough: IVE is I've without its apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosedive is a steep headlong plunge, so taking the plunge describes the dive.

clue.text: Produced in the W. Indies by applying pitch to oil drums?

definitions.text: Produced in the W. Indies by applying pitch to oil drums

parts.words: Produced in the W. Indies by applying pitch to oil drums
parts.note: pitch is musical tuning, not tar, and the drums are tuned oil barrels played in the Caribbean

explanation.surface: Tar applied to oil barrels in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' suggests tar; it means musical tuning. WIndies is the West Indies.
explanation.definitionFit: Caribbean musicians play pans made from oil drums, tuned to notes.

clue.text: Obtain food, say, to give away

explanation.surface: Advice on getting groceries, or perhaps just handing them out.
explanation.definitionFit: To go buying groceries is one sense; to inform on someone, betraying them to the police, is British slang for the other.

clue.text: Hairstyle once associated with type of secretary

explanation.surface: An old hairdo linked to a kind of office worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent wave was the old full name for a perm, and a permanent secretary heads a British civil service department.

clue.text: Unfinished furniture no use for old emperor

indicators.note: unfinished means left without endings, so the last letter goes from each word

parts.note: a commode is a piece of furniture, a chest of drawers or a chair housing a chamber pot

explanation.surface: Incomplete furniture is no good for an ancient ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' docks the final E from COMMODE and from USE; 'no' and 'for' are link words. Commodus was a Roman emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Commodus was a Roman emperor, son of Marcus Aurelius.

clue.text: Is about to be united without fail

indicators.note: without means outside, so the word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to marry is to be united
C stands for circa, about

explanation.surface: A promise to wed without fail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking; MARRY goes round IS and C.
explanation.definitionFit: To miscarry is to go wrong, as a plan miscarries.

clue.text: Ready to attempt finally what no one can play

parts.note: due can mean ready or expected, as in the train is due

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word attempt

explanation.surface: Someone prepared to try at last a piece that nobody is able to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no one' is a pun: nobody alone can play it, since it needs two.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece for two players cannot be performed by one person solo.

clue.text: Actor captivates pit to show his power

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold captive, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: an actor is one who acts, a doer
a pit is a mine

explanation.surface: A performer enthralls the theatre pit, displaying his might on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actor' looks theatrical and 'pit' suggests the stalls, but they are DOER and MINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To domineer is to rule over others overbearingly, exercising authority.

clue.text: Old German museum needs money

parts.note: the V and A is London's Victoria and Albert Museum
L stands for pounds, money

explanation.surface: A museum of old German artefacts needs funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vandals were a Germanic tribe who sacked Rome.

clue.text: Encouragement for boy to speak

indicators.note: to speak suggests the boy's name heard spoken, sounding like another word

parts.note: Philip is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Encouragement given to a child to talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a stimulus or boost.

clue.text: In papal vestment, notice a security device

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, inside the vestment

parts.note: the pallium is a woollen band worn by the Pope
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A church garment worn by the Pope bears a notice about safety equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: The Palladium was the statue of Pallas guarding Troy; by extension, any safeguard.
explanation.definitionFit: A palladium is a safeguard on which protection is thought to depend.

clue.text: Aggressive, though raised up meek

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards

parts.note: meek means shy

explanation.surface: An aggressive person, though meek when confronted.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushy person is assertive in a forceful, aggressive way.

clue.text: Some coconut for a girl clutching a penny

indicators.note: clutching means holding, so the girl's name holds the other piece

parts.note: Cora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl grips a coin, perhaps to buy a bit of coconut.
explanation.definitionFit: Copra is dried coconut kernel, from which oil is pressed.

clue.text: Criticise too heartless a show

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is removed

explanation.surface: A harsh critic calls a show over-cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle O from TOO. A panto, pantomime, is a British Christmas family stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantomime is a traditional British Christmas stage entertainment.

clue.text: Examine boy about offence

parts.note: to scan is to examine closely

indicators.note: about signals turning the word round so it reads backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Inspecting a youth over some misdeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns LAD into DAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is an outrage causing public offence.

clue.text: Cause confusion by a gender change

indicators.note: change tells you to alter the order of these letters

explanation.surface: A person sows disorder by switching sex.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to disorder or throw into disarray.

clue.text: Inarticulate song from Canton?

parts.note: canton is a Swiss district, not the Chinese city, and the wordless warbling sung in Swiss mountains is meant

explanation.surface: A Chinese melody without words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canton' suggests the Chinese city; it is a Swiss canton.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine herdsmen's wordless singing alternates chest voice and falsetto.

clue.text: Don't commit oneself to be a cat's-paw?

explanation.surface: Advice on avoiding commitment and on not being exploited.
explanation.definitionFit: To act cautiously and evasively is one sense; literally a kitten's limb is the other.
